requirements.title: Status waste recorded on the battery passport
requirements.statement: When a battery becomes a waste battery, the system shall record the battery status 'waste' on the battery's passport.

sources.quote: Where the status of a battery changes to that of a waste battery
battery which the holder intends to or is required to discard or discards
The status of the battery must be defined as 'original', 'repurposed', 're-used', 'remanufactured' or 'waste'.

requirements.rationale: DIN DKE SPEC 99100 6.1.3.7 b) lists 'waste' among the statuses of the battery, and Art. 77(7) treats the change to waste as a change of the battery's status. DIN 3.51 says when a battery is waste: when its holder discards it, intends to or is required to. Decision Q-022 (whether waste status and recycling are recorded as separate events) records the status waste when the battery becomes waste, and the recycling as a separate later event that ends the passport (Art. 77(8)).
requirements.acceptance: Test: recording that a battery has become waste sets the status 'waste' on its passport.
requirements.appliesFrom: 18 February 2027 (Art. 77(1)), for each LMT battery, each industrial battery with a capacity greater than 2 kWh and each electric vehicle battery placed on the market or put into service
requirements.notes: Decision Q-022 (whether waste status and recycling are recorded as separate events) decides that the system records the status 'waste' when the battery becomes waste, with the transfer of responsibility of Art. 77(7) second subparagraph, and records recycling as a separate later event that ends the passport (Art. 77(8)).

requirements.title: Preparation for re-use or repurposing only for a waste battery
requirements.statement: The system shall accept preparation for re-use or preparation for repurposing only for a battery whose status is 'waste'.

sources.quote: 'preparation for repurposing' means any operation, by which a waste battery, or parts thereof, is prepared so that it can be used for a different purpose or application than that for which it was originally designed
'preparation for re-use' means preparing for re-use as defined in Article 3, point (16), of Directive 2008/98/EC
processes, by which products or components of products that have become waste are prepared so that they can be re-used without any other pre-processing

requirements.rationale: Both operations are defined on waste: Art. 3(30) on a waste battery, Art. 3(29) through Directive 2008/98/EC, which DIN 3.35 reproduces as products that have become waste. The operations that apply to a battery that is not waste are repurposing (StR-LIFE-015), remanufacturing and repair.
requirements.acceptance: Test: preparation for re-use and preparation for repurposing of a battery whose status is not 'waste' are refused; of a waste battery, accepted.
requirements.appliesFrom: 18 February 2027 (Art. 77(1)), for each LMT battery, each industrial battery with a capacity greater than 2 kWh and each electric vehicle battery placed on the market or put into service
requirements.notes: Decision Q-022 (whether waste status and recycling are recorded as separate events) decides that the system records the status 'waste' when the battery becomes waste and records recycling as a separate later event, so a waste battery that is not yet recycled may still be prepared for re-use or for repurposing.

requirements.title: New passport when a treated battery is placed on the market again
requirements.statement: The system shall create a new battery passport for a battery that has been subject to preparation for re-use, preparation for repurposing, repurposing or remanufacturing and is placed on the market again.

sources.quote: Such battery shall have a new battery passport linked to the battery passport or passports of the original battery or batteries.

A new battery passport must be issued when a battery was subject to remanufacturing, repurpose or one of the treatment operations preparing for re-use and preparing for repurpose and is placed on the market again.

requirements.rationale: Art. 77(7) and DIN 6.1.3.7 e) require a new passport; Art. 3(1) counts a battery that has undergone these operations as a battery in its own right. A new passport after preparation for re-use, preparation for repurposing, repurposing or remanufacturing is model B of the vision (invariant 5, ADR 0003). Repair is the only exception (SyR-LIFE-041).
requirements.acceptance: Demonstration and test for each of the four operations: the treated battery placed on the market again has a new passport, distinct from the original one.
requirements.appliesFrom: 18 February 2027 (Art. 77(1)), for each LMT battery, each industrial battery with a capacity greater than 2 kWh and each electric vehicle battery placed on the market or put into service

requirements.rationale: DIN adds the repair history to the status; under model A it is the only record of what a repair changed on the same passport.
requirements.acceptance: Test: two repairs on one battery give two entries in its repair history, each with its date and its treatment.
requirements.notes: StR-LIFE-045 depends on Q-030 (the access tier for a battery's repair history). Decision Q-045 (the role that records a repair) names, in the data layer, the company that holds the value-chain role repairer as the writer of the repair record (SyR-LIFE-044); the EU regulatory role of the passport demo stays with follow-up FS14 (repair on the same passport).

requirements.title: Rated capacity recorded at placing and at each status change
requirements.statement: The battery passport dataset shall contain the rated capacity (in Ah) of the individual battery recorded when it is placed on the market and again at each change of its status, keeping each earlier value.

sources.quote: (a) the values for performance and durability parameters referred to in Article 10(1), when the battery is placed on the market and when it is subject to changes in its status;

rechargeable industrial batteries with a capacity greater than 2 kWh, LMT batteries and electric vehicle batteries shall be accompanied by a document containing values for the electrochemical performance and durability parameters set out in Part A of Annex IV.
Rated capacity (in Ah) and capacity fade (in %).
The update interval shall be upon placement on the market and change of status.
the values for performance and durability parameters referred to in Article 10(1), when the battery is placed on the market and when it is subject to changes in its status
shall be accompanied by a document containing values for the electrochemical performance and durability parameters set out in Part A of Annex IV.
1. Rated capacity (in Ah) and capacity fade (in %).
The update interval must be upon placement on the market and change of status.
The update interval must be upon placement on the market and upon change of the battery status
The energy round trip efficiency fade must be updated upon placement on the market and change of the battery status
The internal resistance increase must be updated upon change of the battery status

requirements.rationale: Annex XIII point 4(a) asks for the Annex IV Part A values at the placing on the market and at each change of status. Under model B the change of status comes with a new passport, which carries the new value; under model A (repair) the same passport carries both. The earlier values stay, because the point names both moments.
requirements.acceptance: Test: a battery placed on the market and later repaired shows on its passport the value at placing and the value at the repair; after it becomes waste and is prepared for re-use, the new passport carries the new value and the original passport keeps its values.
requirements.appliesFrom: Art. 10(1): from 18 August 2024 for the accompanying document; in the battery passport from 18 February 2027 (Art. 77(1))
requirements.notes: Kept over StR-LIFE-089 (integration review pass-life), whose sources are merged here. DIN DKE SPEC 99100 relates these parameters to the battery model and does not ask for a value of the individual battery at each change of status; the Regulation does (Annex XIII point 4(a)). Art. 10(4) disapplies Art. 10(1) to (3) to a treated battery whose original battery was placed on the market or put into service before the dates of those paragraphs (StR-LIFE-115). The access tier is StR-PASS-252.

catenaXCompliance.note: BatteryPass 6.1.0 (the CX-Titan battery passport aspect model) performance.rated.capacity.value (rated capacity in ampere-hours), and the Industrial Digital Twin Association (IDTA) Technical Data IDTA-02035-4 RatedCapacity (in Ah) of CX-0160 1.1.0 (the CX-Neptune Battery Passport standard) carry one value per passport. Neither release keeps the value recorded at placing on the market beside the values recorded at each later change of status; with a new passport per status change the earlier value remains only in the predecessor passport, which BatteryPass links and CX-Neptune does not.

history.reason: SYS.1 elicitation, area lifecycle

Both require the rated capacity of the individual battery in the dataset at placing on the market and at each change of status (Annex XIII point 4(a), Art. 10(1), Annex IV Part A); one test (place a battery, change its status, inspect the values) passes or fails both. StR-LIFE-089 is kept: it is more precise (it states that each earlier value is kept, and its acceptance covers both the repair on the same passport and the new passport of model B) and better sourced (it adds the DIN update clause where DIN has one and the project rule of the project guidelines of the battery passport application). The access tier of these values stays with StR-PASS-252. StR-PASS-242 carried EU-ART10 and EU-ANNEX13-025 identifiers: the EU-ART10 one stays claimed by the model-level passport-content requirement, EU-ANNEX13-025 moves to lifecycle.
integration review
Carries over the context note of the rejected duplicate StR-PASS-242.

Not atomic (six values in one shall) and fully covered: the update at placing on the market and at each change of status of the rated capacity, capacity fade, power fade, energy round trip efficiency fade, internal resistance increase and expected lifetime in calendar years is stated one value each by StR-LIFE-089, StR-LIFE-090, StR-LIFE-092, StR-LIFE-096, StR-LIFE-094 and StR-LIFE-098, which quote the same DIN clauses and Annex XIII point 4(a). The test of StR-PASS-232 (after a status change the values are set for the new status and the values at placing stay readable) is the test of those six. Its sources are merged into the six, each with its own DIN clause.
